memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"Then the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar. They shall remove all the fat, just as the fat is removed from the lamb of the fellowship offering, and the priest shall burn it on the altar on top of the food offerings presented to the LORD. In this way the priest will make atonement for them for the sin they have committed, and they will be forgiven."'" - Lev 4:34-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
For the fourth and final time, the chapter closes with the same words: and they will be forgiven.

Priest. Community. Leader. Ordinary person. Four kinds of sinner, four sacrifices of different sizes, one identical verdict.

Stand back and look at what Leviticus 4 has done. It has methodically walked through every category of person in Israel and made sure that not one of them is left without provision. Nobody reads this chapter and thinks, there is no way back for me.

That is the heart of God, written into law thousands of years before Calvary.

And notice the phrase in verse 35: burned on top of the food offerings. Once again, the sin offering rests on what was already burning. Grace was there before the sin was.

Then read what Hebrews says about all of this: those sacrifices are an annual reminder of sins, because it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins (Heb 10:3-4). The system was never the solution. It was the promise of one.

Christ has appeared once for all at the culmination of the ages to do away with sin by the sacrifice of himself (Heb 9:26).

Four times God said "forgiven" to Israel. In Christ, He says it over you — and it does not need repeating.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I trusting in a finished sacrifice, or still trying to add something to it?
2. Which of the four categories in this chapter do I most identify with — and have I brought my sin to Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Leviticus left no one without a way back, and that Christ has completed what those sacrifices could only promise. I rest in His finished work today. Amen.
